1.explanation:
• UIShell/README.md – gives the overall structure of the UI Shell, including how SkipToContent and the Header/Naviga­tion subcomponents fit together.  
• UIShell/SkipToContent.js – contains the actual implementation and styling of the “Skip to main” link; you’ll need to inspect and update its colors to fix contrast.  
• Link/index.js – SkipToContent is built on Carbon’s Link component, so you’ll want to see default Link styling (hover/focus states) and override rules.  
• UIShell/HeaderNavigation.js – renders the <nav> and <ul> that should receive role="menubar" (or menu) to contain menuitems.  
• UIShell/HeaderMenu.js – in horizontal mode this wraps groups of menu items; it’s a good place to apply or forward the proper role.  
• UIShell/HeaderMenuItem.js – attaches role="menuitem" to each anchor. Understanding this file shows why DAP flags it and where to conditionally add or remove ARIA roles.
1.bug_scenario:
When you load the Carbon React UI Shell’s Header Base with Navigation (or Navigation + Actions) in Chrome and run the IBM DAP accessibility tool (July 2019 ruleset), two types of violations pop up:

1. Contrast error on the “Skip to main content” link: that link is rendered as white text on a relatively light background, giving a contrast ratio (~1.9:1) that fails WCAG A (14 px weight 400 requires at least 4.5:1).

2. A WAI-ARIA role error in the Header navigation: each <HeaderMenuItem> anchor has role="menuitem" but its container isn’t marked with role="menu", "menubar" or "group". DAP only surfaces it when the browser width is narrow (so the menu collapses into the side nav). The screenshot shows the DOM: a <nav> with class “bx--side-nav__navigation” wrapping a <ul> of items, but no menu/menubar role on the parent, so the children’s menuitem role is invalid.
